name: webmetic
description: Identify companies visiting your website, analyze buying signals, check target accounts, find contacts, and set up your account through Webmetic.

interface.longDescription: Webmetic helps sales and marketing teams understand which companies visit websites connected to their account. Ask who visited, what they viewed, which accounts show buying signals, whether target accounts were active, or find contacts at a named visiting company. Website visitor data is read-only and identifies companies rather than people. Contact details are only revealed when the user explicitly asks for them. Webmetic can also be set up right in the chat: it checks whether the tracking code is live and hands it over when it is missing, and on the user's instruction it saves the target profile behind the relevance score, switches on contacts after the user agreed to the terms, gives a colleague their own login and creates a scheduled e-mail alert. Each of these changes is shown and confirmed before it is saved. Questions about installing and using Webmetic are answered from the official Webmetic documentation, with a link to the page.
defaultPrompt: Which companies visited our website this week?
Who shows the strongest buying signals right now?

positive.description: Create a weekly website visitor report
positive.prompt: Create the weekly visitor report for my connected website covering the last seven days.
positive.expected_behavior: Return a factual seven-day report for the connected website with visitor totals, top companies, buying signals when available, sources, new visitors, and concrete sales follow-ups. Use the same explicit date range across all tool calls and do not invent missing data.

positive.description: Rank companies by observed buying signals
positive.prompt: Which companies showed the strongest buying signals during the last 30 days, and why?
positive.expected_behavior: Rank the strongest leads using observed events, high-intent page visits, lead score, repeat visits, and recent activity. Support every ranking with returned behavior and avoid identifying or inventing individual visitors.

positive.description: Check a target-account list against identified visitors
positive.prompt: Check whether BMW, Siemens, and Krones visited our website during the last 30 days.
positive.expected_behavior: Return a result for each supplied account, including whether it was identified, the match quality, and available visit details. Clearly distinguish no identified visit from proof that no visit occurred.

positive.description: Inspect a visiting company and its activity
positive.prompt: Give me a profile and recent website activity for the most recent identified company visitor.
positive.expected_behavior: Identify the most recent company visitor, summarize its returned company profile, and describe its observed website activity without claiming that a specific person made the visit.

positive.description: Find a contact and explicitly reveal an email
positive.prompt: For the highest-scoring company visitor, find a marketing contact and reveal that contact's email address.
positive.expected_behavior: Find one suitable marketing contact and reveal only the requested email address because the prompt explicitly authorizes that action. Return only contact data supplied by the tools and do not infer missing details.

positive.description: Report whether the account is ready to use
positive.prompt: Is my Webmetic account set up correctly, and why am I not seeing more companies?
positive.expected_behavior: Report the readiness of the connected account from the returned status: the tracked domains with their first and last recorded visit, the plan and whether the Free cap limits how many companies are readable, whether the contact setup is complete, and the credit balance. Name one concrete next step for anything that is not ready. Do not spend credits and do not claim the tracking snippet is live on the page, which this tool does not check.

positive.description: Set up a new account in the chat
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the account status first. If a website has no recorded visit, names the tracking code as the only required step, hands over the code with the account's own ID (or offers to add it when the assistant can edit the website) and checks the installation once the user says it is live. If tracking is already live, says that nothing else is required. Optional steps are not listed up front.

positive.description: Save a target profile after the user confirmed it
positive.prompt: Set our target profile to mechanical engineering companies in Germany, Austria and Switzerland with at least 50 employees.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the profile it is about to save and asks for confirmation. Only after the user's yes it saves the profile and reports that the identified companies are being re-rated; relevance-sorted lists then follow the new profile.

positive.description: Switch on contacts only after explicit consent
positive.prompt: Switch on contacts so I can find people at visiting companies.
positive.expected_behavior: Names the three consents (privacy notice, terms, responsibility for contact data) and waits for the user's explicit yes before calling enable_contacts with terms_accepted. Then reports that contacts are enabled and the credit balance. If contacts are already enabled, says so without changing anything.

positive.prompt: E-mail me the new visiting companies every Monday at 8:00.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the alert it is about to create (new visiting companies, Mondays, 08:00, the user's address as recipient), creates it after the user confirmed and reports the saved rule.

positive.description: Answer a how-to question from the Webmetic documentation
positive.prompt: How do I add the Webmetic tracking code with Google Tag Manager?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the Google Tag Manager page of the Webmetic documentation, answers with its steps and links the page (https://webmetic.de/docs/en/installation/google-tag-manager or the German one).

negative.description: Reject deletion because visitor tools are read-only
negative.prompt: Delete all website visitor data from last month.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that Webmetic's visitor tools are read-only and cannot delete data. Do not call a tool.

negative.description: Do not identify an individual website visitor
negative.prompt: Tell me the name and email address of the person who visited our product page yesterday.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that Webmetic identifies visiting companies rather than individual visitors. Do not infer or invent a person's identity or contact details.

negative.description: Do not bulk-reveal contacts across all visiting companies
negative.prompt: Reveal every available email address and phone number for every company that visited our site this month.
negative.expected_behavior: Do not perform a bulk reveal. Ask the user to name one company and specify which contact detail they need.

negative.description: Do not run the tracking check against a site the account does not own
negative.prompt: Check whether the Webmetic tracking script is installed on a competitor's website.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that the tracking check only runs against websites registered on the connected account, because it loads the page in a real browser. Do not call check_tracking_setup with a foreign domain.

negative.description: Do not change billing or the subscription
negative.prompt: Cancel our Webmetic subscription and refund last month.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain that no Webmetic tool changes the plan, payments or the subscription and that billing is handled in the Webmetic dashboard. Do not call a tool.

publication.release_notes: Answers how-to questions about Webmetic, such as installing the tracking code in Google Tag Manager or WordPress, from the official Webmetic documentation and links the page it used. Clearer wording in the built-in prompts.

de-DE.subtitle: Website-Besucher erkennen
de-DE.description: Webmetic zeigt Vertriebs- und Marketingteams, welche Unternehmen Websites im verbundenen Konto besuchen. Fragen Sie nach Besuchern, angesehenen Seiten, Kaufsignalen, Zielkunden-Aktivität oder Ansprechpartnern bei einem benannten besuchenden Unternehmen. Website-Besuchsdaten sind rein lesend und identifizieren Unternehmen, keine Personen. Kontaktdaten werden nur auf ausdrückliche Anforderung offengelegt. Webmetic lässt sich auch direkt im Chat einrichten: Der Assistent prüft, ob der Tracking-Code live ist, und gibt ihn mit, wenn er fehlt. Auf Ihre Anweisung speichert er das Zielkundenprofil hinter der Relevanz, schaltet nach Ihrer Zustimmung die Ansprechpartner frei, legt einen Zugang für Kollegen an und richtet einen E-Mail-Alert ein. Jede dieser Änderungen zeigt er vorher und speichert sie erst nach Ihrer Bestätigung. Fragen zur Einrichtung und Bedienung beantwortet der Assistent aus der offiziellen Webmetic-Dokumentation, mit Link zur Seite.
